## `pm:retriage` — execution-seat dissent on the *route*, not on the diagnosis

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`.
⛔ No label removed — `pm:retriage` is attached **alongside** `pm:queue`, per the standing
convention, and it is what keeps this card out of dispatch while the dissent is undecided. I am
not re-grading: `domain:*`, `type` and grading belong to the triage seat alone.

⚠️ Recording it here also repairs a half-state of my own making: I reached this conclusion in
the seat's working thread and never wrote it onto the card. A conclusion that lives only in chat
is not a state — and this card sat in the dispatchable queue in the meantime, where my own next
round could legitimately have picked it up.

### What I agree with

The diagnosis. `PartialSchema<T>` collapses to one property for every instantiation, it is a
convenience alias rather than a capability, and "declared, published, collapsed, and unpinned"
is indeed the one state that must not survive this card. Option 2 is correctly not chartered.

### The dissent: the return path cannot fire

The charter conditions shipping option 1 on a return path:

> Return path: **any signal of an out-of-tree consumer**, or a removal route that would require
> semver-major, ⇒ `needs_decision` rather than shipping.

⭐ For a **type-only export of a published package**, this repo has no instrument that can emit
that signal. The census the card rests on measures `packages/`, `apps/`, `examples/`,
`content/docs` — every consumer it can see is one that lives here. An out-of-tree consumer is,
by construction, invisible to all of them. So the guard reads as a safety condition but is
unfireable: the default (retire) wins by absence of evidence rather than by evidence of absence.

That is the same shape I ruled against on #6394 — a condition that can never be satisfied is not
a condition, and a green that no mechanism could have turned red is not a measurement.

### Why this lands on the human floor

Removing a published export is a **breaking removal of a published capability**, which the
standing floor reserves for the maintainer regardless of how the four facets fall. Two things
that do **not** move it off that floor:

- **"It's degenerate, so nobody can be using it meaningfully."** True of the *semantics*,
  irrelevant to the *break*. An out-of-tree file that writes `import type { PartialSchema }` stops
  compiling whether or not the type was useful — the collapse makes it a bad alias, not an absent
  one.
- **"The route is a `minor` under the no-`major` convention."** That changes the notice period,
  not what is removed. A convention that forbids `major` bumps does not convert a breaking
  removal into a non-breaking one; it means the break ships under a `minor`, which is a stronger
  reason for a human to sign it, not a weaker one.

### What I propose, so this is not a block

Split the card along the line the charter already draws:

1. **Ship option 3 now, in this lane.** Pin the collapse so the alias cannot be silently adopted,
   plus the explicit sequencing note behind #5155. That is additive, breaks nothing, needs no
   ruling, and it retires the dangerous state — "declared, published, collapsed, and *unpinned*"
   — today. I can dispatch it this round.
2. **Send the retirement half to the decision box** as its own card, with the four-facet block,
   and let the maintainer rule on removing a published export.

If the triage seat rules that a type-only export under a `minor` is outside the floor, I will
take that ruling and dispatch option 1 as chartered — the dissent is on the record, not a veto.
What I will not do is dispatch a removal of a published export on a guard that cannot fire.

## Claimed + dispatched under the narrowed charter

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`,
branch `claude/issue-6397-partialschema-collapse-pin`.

Triage upheld the dissent in substance: the retirement half is off this card and stays on the
human floor; what is chartered today is the **option-3 floor** — pin the collapse, plus the
explicit sequencing note behind #5155. `pm:retriage` cleared, `pm:queue` + Task stand.

⭐ **Triage's ruling improved on what I proposed, and the improvement is the interesting part.**
I asked for the retirement half to go to the decision box now. Triage declined, and gave a better
reason than I had: **once #5155 lands, the alias works as written and the removal question
dissolves** — escalating today would spend the maintainer's attention on a question #5155 is
expected to moot, while the pin already retires the one genuinely impermissible state,
*"declared, published, collapsed, and unpinned."* If retirement is still wanted after #5155, that
is a fresh enforce-or-remove card and it goes to the maintainer then. I am taking that as the
charter.

### Scope — additive only

1. A **checker-level pin** asserting the one-declared-property reading of `PartialSchema<T>`, so
   the alias cannot be silently adopted as protection it does not provide.
2. The explicit **sequencing note behind #5155**.

⛔ **Do not retire, deprecate, or narrow `PartialSchema`.** Removing a published export of
`@object-ui/types` is a breaking removal of published capability and sits on the human floor —
upheld by triage, not open for a dev or this seat to reinterpret. ⛔ No `@deprecated` tag either:
that is a step on the retirement path, not a pin.

### Pre-dispatch gate

- **(a) Whole thread read** — 4 records: triage's original charter, my dissent, triage's
  re-judgement, and this claim.
- **(b) Shadow check, in-flight and batch.** `packages/types` is touched by #6373 in the same
  batch — but at **`src/data-display.ts`** (`TableColumn`), a different file from where
  `PartialSchema` lives. Also in flight: #6034 (`app-shell`), #6038 (predicate-fault warning).
  ⚠️ Re-derive the file surface on your branch and **stop and report** if your pin needs to touch
  `data-display.ts`.
- **(c) Call-site census** — yours to run: every in-repo instantiation of `PartialSchema<T>`, so
  the pin asserts the collapse against real usage rather than a synthetic type.

### Ghost-assertion guard — the trap is specific here

A pin on a **collapsed** type is easy to write vacuously: an assertion that passes both when the
type collapses *and* when it does not is decoration. Prove it fails — construct the
non-collapsed shape (or the shape `PartialSchema` would have if `keyof T` resolved as its author
intended), show the pin **red** against it, and quote both readings. State the predicted direction
before each run and restore by **hash**, not exit code.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**, and the open question is ruled **A** (keep `patch`)

PR #6433, head `2ec7800b0`. `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session
`session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. Verified on a pinned ref (`refs/pmtmp/6397`).

### The ⛔ that mattered most: additive only — verified mechanically, not read

The narrowed charter forbade retiring, removing, deprecating or narrowing the export. I checked it
the way the claim deserves: every `+`/`-` line in the `packages/types/src/index.ts` diff filtered
against "starts with `*`, `/**`, or `*/`" returns **empty**.

**The whole production diff is inside a JSDoc block.** The declaration at `:905` is byte-identical,
no `@deprecated` tag, no export added or removed. That is exactly the shape triage chartered.

### The census is zero, and the card's second hit was a build artifact

`PartialSchema` on `origin/main`, tracked files, `dist/` excluded: **exactly one occurrence
repo-wide** — the declaration itself. Zero in-repo instantiations.

⭐ The card recorded a second hit; the dev identified it as the package's own emitted
`dist/index.d.ts`, which is absent from a fresh worktree. My grep needed an explicit `grep -v
/dist/` to reproduce the clean reading, which corroborates it. **A build artifact counted as a
usage** is a small but real census error, and finding it is why the pin's four subject types are
the card's measured ones with the synthetic type demoted to a control — rather than a pin built on
a usage that does not exist.

Positive control on the same pathspec (`ObjectViewSchema`, multiple files) confirms the zero is a
real zero and not a broken query.

⚠️ It also corrected one of the card's numbers: `ObjectViewSchema` is recorded as "27+"; measured
today it is **42**, and **27 is `ButtonSchema`**. A number carried forward from a card is worth
re-measuring; that one was attached to the wrong type.

### The ablations do what I asked, and Ablation 1 is the right counterfactual

I asked for the **non-collapsed shape** — what `PartialSchema` would produce if `keyof T` resolved
as its author intended — and for the pin to go red against it.

**Ablation 1** removes `[key: string]: any` from `BaseSchema`, i.e. the #5155 counterfactual.
Predicted: counts jump from `["type"]` to the source counts, every `stringIndex` assertion flips.
Observed exactly that — `17 failed | 14 passed`, with 61/67/42/27 declared instead of `["type"]`.
⭐ And the 14 that stayed green are **the instrument and the control**, which never depended on
that index signature — so the split itself demonstrates the pin is measuring the collapse rather
than the file loading.

**Ablation 2** (retire the alias) reds at section 0 with the probe import unresolved.

Both legs from a committed tree, mutation proven on disk (grep counts of removed *and* injected
text plus a changed `git hash-object`), restored under a trap with absolute paths and verified
**by hash** (`git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` == `git hash-object <path>`), `git diff HEAD` empty.
Directions predicted correctly on both.

Pin-in-program proved rather than assumed: `tsc -p … --listFiles`, 511 files, pin at line 363.

### Ruling on the open question — **A, keep `patch`**

The question was `patch` vs empty frontmatter for a change whose only published effect is a JSDoc
note.

**A.** The dev's distinction is correct and it is evidence-backed: the `.changeset/4850-…`
precedent covered **eslint directives, which never reach a `.d.ts`**. This note does — confirmed
on a real `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`, emitted at `dist/index.d.ts:130`.

⭐ And it follows from the charter rather than from taste: triage chartered this pin so the alias
**"cannot be silently adopted as protection."** A warning that never ships to the published
declaration a consumer reads cannot do that job. An empty-frontmatter changeset would leave the
guard working in-repo and invisible to the only people it is meant to warn.

Raising it as non-blocking with a recommendation and shipping the defensible option, rather than
stopping for a ruling on a one-line flip, was the right call on scope too.

### Landing

⛔ Not enqueued — 18 green, **10 still running**, 0 failures, `behind` (⛔ not syncing; it resolves
unaided here).
